children.text: by: Chloe Westerman and Steven Alexander

Medical influencers, or “medfluencers,” are a popular subset of social media influencers that utilize their status as health professionals or aspirations of working in the medical field to discuss and advise an audience on lifestyle, health, and wellness. Professionalism is a standard that doctors and prospective doctors ought to follow when acting under the public eye. Additional considerations should be made online while discussing lifestyle recommendations, accepting sponsorship deals, and determining how information will be perceived or potentially misunderstood by an audience. Professionalism as a standard is exhibited by both Melissa Qin and Dr. Mike through their emphasis on self-hygiene and wellness; for instance, through pilates, boxing, or other physical activities, they demonstrate behaviors consistent with those who practice medicine. In addition, they both present themselves in a polished manner through dignified verbiage and work-appropriate attire. As doctors and future doctors, social media has blurred the line between occupation and personal life, especially for those who are bound by ethical constraints, beneficence, and non-maleficence. We argue that medical mavens should act with additional caution when operating under the public eye, and refrain from credentialism.

Melissa Qin is a Harvard Medical student and social media influencer. She describes herself in her TikTok bio as a “fashion addict & harvard med m2,” with her personal brand involving being a successful medical student who also balances time for regular exercise, self-care, and a curated fashion sense. Her content style rotates between medical student content and lifestyle content, including anything between fashion, travel, and her personal life. She often blurs the line between these two niches, posting popular trend videos with a medical student slant. She is considered a macroinfluencer on TikTok, with 111.2K followers. Melissa’s intended audience is pre-medical and medical students looking for advice to maintain a healthy lifestyle while also managing a rigorous course load. However, some comments on her medical school posts state “I have ZERO medical knowledge/schooling but would love to hear someone nerd out about it everyday. Makes it more exciting hearing it so passionately from another person than reading about it🤷🏻‍♀️,” and “me listening to this whole video while in architecture school.” As a whole, she attracts an actual audience who may or may not be interested in the medical field but are curious to learn more about it, and individuals who enjoy viewing her lifestyle content outside of medicine.

Dr. Mike: "I’m not used to getting this passionate on camera but sometimes it’s warranted"

Mikhail Oskarovich Varshavski, popularly known as Dr. Mike, is a prominent medical influencer (or Medfluencer) with 3 million followers on TikTok, 5.6 million followers on Instagram, and 15 million subscribers on YouTube. Originally a board-certified family medicine physician and osteopathic doctor (DO), Dr. Mike began his more notable career as an influencer after People magazine dubbed him the "Sexiest Doctor Alive" in 2015. He moved from Russia to New York when he was 6 years old, where he spent the remainder of his formative years. Dr. Mike received his education at the New York Institute of Technology College of Osteopathic Medicine—through a joint undergraduate and medical educational program—and currently practices through Atlantic Health System in Chatham, New Jersey. Through debates, podcasts, and public speeches, Dr. Mike centers his brand and personal image on debunking medical misinformation, offering evidence-based wellness information, and occasionally producing lifestyle videos and brand sponsorships.

Caption: “I’m not used to getting this passionate on camera but sometimes it’s warranted 😡I’ve seen patients hurt by our shitty healthcare system and instead of addressing these real (and fixable) issues, we’re wasting time chasing ghosts (banning food dyes) 😮‍💨🙏🏼❤️”
